answers.answer: Each player starts with 25 money, 1 active worker on the notepad and 3 inactive workers below it, draws 8 Zoo cards and keeps 4 (discarding 4), and draws 2 Final Scoring cards. All five Action cards start side I up; Animals goes in the leftmost slot (strength 1) and the other four are randomly placed in the remaining slots. Appeal starts at 0 for the first player, 1 for the second, 2 for the third, and 3 for the fourth.
answers.evidence: Personal setup B–G: Animals card under the leftmost slot; 1 worker active and 3 lying down; 25 money; 2 Final Scoring cards; draw 8, keep 4; Appeal track staggered 0–3 by turn order.

answers.answer: With 2 players, place 3 Base Conservation Project cards face up and block the left level on the left card, middle level on the middle card, right level on the right card, plus the three spaces in the donation area's left column; neither player can use these blocked spaces. With 3 players, place 3 face-up base projects and there are no setup blocks specified. With 4 players, place 4 face-up base projects and there are no setup blocks specified. Reveal the 6-card display after everyone has chosen their starting hand cards.
answers.evidence: Setup 5b–5c: 4 projects in a 4-player game, otherwise 3; only the 2-player setup covers the specified levels and donation spaces. Setup G reveals the display after hand selection.

answers.answer: After using a card in slot 4, remove it, shift the cards that were to its left (slots 1–3) one slot to the right, and put the used card in slot 1. Set action strength before performing the action. Each X-token spent adds 1 strength and returns to the supply; any number may be spent, but you can hold at most 5 X-tokens, and tokens gained during the action cannot boost that same action. Resolve an 'after finishing' effect after completing the action, including moving the Action cards.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: remove the used card, shift cards left of the empty slot right, place used card in slot 1; strength set before action; each X-token adds +1; after-finishing effects follow card movement.

answers.answer: Yes. If you cannot or do not want to perform one of the five actions, choose an Action card and take exactly 1 X-token instead. Move that card to slot 1 and shift intervening cards right; its strength and upgrade side do not matter. You cannot take this action if you already hold 5 X-tokens.
answers.evidence: X-token action: take exactly 1 X-token, still select and move an Action card to slot 1, and the action is unavailable at 5 X-tokens.

answers.answer: When the Break token reaches the last space, ignore additional movement beyond that space. The break happens after the current turn ends, and reaching the last space gives the triggering player 1 X-token. The current player completes the turn before the break; after the break, the token resets to the player-count start space and play continues clockwise with the next player. The summary does not specify a different next-turn order beyond that.
answers.evidence: Break track: break after the end of the current turn, 1 X-token for reaching the last space, ignore extra steps, reset after break; break procedure says play continues clockwise with the next player.

answers.answer: Cards I advances the Break token 2 spaces, then either draws from the deck according to the slot-strength table (up to 3, with a possible discard) or snaps exactly 1 display card at strength 5 or more, regardless of reputation. Cards II also advances the Break token 2 spaces, then draws from the deck and/or display cards within reputation range in any order according to the upgraded table; a strength-3-or-more snap takes 1 card, and higher strength does not improve that snap. Display cards taken are replenished only after the turn is complete. The hand limit is checked at breaks, normally 3 or 5 with the relevant university; there is no in-turn hand limit.
answers.evidence: Cards action I/II states the 2-space movement, deck and snap options and thresholds; display refill is at turn end; hand limit applies during breaks only.

answers.answer: Reputation range includes the display card in the folder matching your Reputation counter and every lower-numbered folder. Reputation 10 or higher requires the upgraded Cards action. At reputation 15, additional reputation does not move the counter and instead gives 1 appeal per excess reputation step. You may not look through the discard pile during the game.
answers.evidence: Reputation track and display defines range as the matching folder and lower folders, requires upgraded Cards for 10+, converts gains beyond 15 to appeal, and prohibits looking through the discard pile.

answers.answer: Build I builds exactly 1 building with size no greater than action strength. Build II builds any number of different buildings, with total size no greater than strength, and no two identical buildings in that action. Buildings cost 2 money per space; on Build II pay separately for each before placing it. The first building must have at least one space on a map border; later buildings must touch an existing building by at least one edge. Build only on empty spaces, cannot extend off-map, overlap, or cover water/rock; restricted-icon spaces require upgraded Build. Every kiosk must be at least 3 spaces from every other kiosk. Each pavilion gives 1 appeal immediately, once. Covering a placement-bonus space grants that bonus immediately.
answers.evidence: Build action and placement rules: exactly one vs. different buildings, size and cost rules, border/adjacency requirements, prohibited spaces, kiosk distance, pavilion appeal, and placement bonuses.

answers.answer: Build I offers kiosks, pavilions, standard enclosures, and the Petting Zoo (size 3; maximum one per zoo). Build II additionally offers the Reptile House and Large Bird Aviary (each size 5; maximum one of each per zoo). The components list has four of each special-enclosure type. Build cannot create unique buildings; those enter only through Sponsor cards. Covering every map space except water and rock immediately gives 7 appeal.
answers.evidence: Build I lists its available buildings and Petting Zoo limit; Build II adds the two size-5 houses and excludes unique buildings; Components lists 4 each; full map gives 7 appeal.

answers.answer: The summary explicitly says that money gained for playing an animal pays out later, so you must be able to pay that animal's full cost first. Build II says to pay separately for each building before placing it. It does not give a general rule for whether money or other bonuses gained during an action can pay for a later building or association task in that same action, so that broader timing question is unsupported. Immediate effects resolve during the action; Animal 'after finishing' effects wait until the whole Animals action is complete and the Action card has moved to slot 1. Simultaneous effects are ordered by the owning player. Build II placement bonuses are taken before building the next building, while 'after finishing' bonuses wait until the whole Build action is complete.
answers.evidence: Animal costs must be payable before money-gain effects; Build II pays each building before placing; immediate and after-finishing effects have separate timing; owning player orders simultaneous effects. No general later-cost funding rule is stated.

answers.answer: For each animal, meet all conditions on its card, then pay its cost. A partner zoo on the animal's continent reduces cost by 3 money for each continent icon on that card. Animals other than Petting Zoo animals may each occupy an empty standard enclosure at least the indicated size; flip it to its occupied side. Required adjacent water/rock spaces must also be met. Petting Zoo animals can go only in the Petting Zoo. All reptiles and some birds may instead use their corresponding special enclosure if eligible; water/rock conditions also apply there. Mark the number of special-enclosure spaces shown on the animal card with your tokens, and the animal cannot be housed there without enough free capacity; special enclosures are never flipped. Resolve ordinary effects immediately, including before playing a second animal; 'after finishing' effects wait until the Animals action is complete. With two animals, finish the first animal's steps before the second.
answers.evidence: Animals action steps specify conditions, payment and the per-icon partner discount, empty-enclosure size and adjacency, special-enclosure eligibility and token capacity, and effect timing.

answers.answer: Animals II allows animals from the display within reputation range as well as from hand; pay an additional cost equal to the display folder number. The two animals may be any mix of hand and display, and the display is not replenished until the turn ends. At strength 5 or more, you may increase reputation by 1 at the very beginning of the action, so the higher range applies. You may also play animals whose conditions show the upgrade-required icon.
answers.evidence: Animals II: display play within range with folder-number cost, mixed sources, no refill until turn end, strength-5 reputation gain at action start, and upgrade-required conditions allowed.

answers.answer: Moving animals from standard enclosures into a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary is allowed only immediately when that house is built, and only once per building. All reptiles may use the Reptile House and some birds may use the Large Bird Aviary, according to their cards; you may move as many eligible animals as capacity permits. For each animal, mark the number of spaces shown on its card with player tokens, and it cannot move there if insufficient capacity remains. The smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting that animal's requirements, including water/rock adjacency, is flipped back to empty. The summary gives no fallback procedure if no such standard enclosure can be freed.
answers.evidence: Moving animals into a new special enclosure: only immediately on building and once per building; flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting requirements; mark the special enclosure with the suitable number of tokens. Animal rules say insufficient free spaces prevents placement.

answers.answer: The summary names four Association tasks (increase reputation, gain partner zoo, gain university, and conservation-project work) but does not state their individual strength values, so those values are unsupported. Association I performs exactly one task, requires at least one active worker, and requires action strength at least the task's strength. If one of your workers is already on that task, place two workers; if three of your workers are there, you cannot do it again until after the break. Other players' workers do not matter. Association II can perform one or more different tasks, using one or two of your workers per task, with total task value no greater than action strength.
answers.evidence: Association I/II gives the task list, one-task versus different multiple-task limits, worker and repeat-task requirements, other-player rule, and total-strength rule; no numerical task strengths are given.

answers.answer: Partner zoos and universities are taken from the Association board and placed bottom-up in the corresponding spaces on your zoo map; printed bonuses on spaces covered are taken immediately. At breaks, replenish each so it is available exactly once, skipping any already held by all players. Partner zoos must be from different continents and are limited to 4; the third and fourth require upgraded Association. Universities cannot be duplicated. A university showing reputation advances your Reputation counter, and universities are the only way to raise the hand limit to 5 (otherwise it is 3, enforced at breaks).
answers.evidence: Association tasks describe taking partner zoos/universities from the board, map placement and bonuses, distinct-continent and no-duplicate rules; break procedure replenishes; the map and hand-limit text set partner and hand limits.

answers.answer: A project can already be in play, or be played from hand as part of conservation-project work and supported immediately; Association II also permits playing a new project directly from the display within reputation range, paying its folder number. To support, meet an uncovered condition and place one of your player tokens from the left edge of your zoo map on it; each player may support each project only once. The token activates its map bonus, which is taken immediately; you choose whether to take it before or after the project reward. A new project goes in the leftmost space above the board and pushes existing projects right. If it exceeds the player-count limit, discard the rightmost project; tokens on it return to their owners' supplies, while the bonuses already activated on their zoo maps stay activated. Base projects do not move.
answers.evidence: Association conservation-project work and support rules describe hand/display entry, conditions and once limit, token source and bonus timing; overflow projects and token destinations are specified.

answers.answer: A release requires discarding an animal with the specific icon that requires a standard enclosure of the depicted size; the summary says whether it could also live in a special enclosure is irrelevant. It does not explicitly say 'exactly' in describing the size match. Move Appeal back by the animal's appeal value, free the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting its requirements (including water/rock), or remove the appropriate tokens from its special enclosure, and discard the Animal card. Since project icon-counting uses icons on cards in front of you, removing the animal removes it from those card counts. The summary does not specify a separate loss of reputation or conservation points from releasing it; the project support reward is whatever the project depicts (including reputation if shown).
answers.evidence: Release into the wild: animal with specific icon, standard enclosure of depicted size, appeal counter moves back by animal appeal, free a qualifying enclosure or remove special-enclosure tokens, and discard the card. Project support rewards are depicted; icon counts use cards in front of you. No separate reputation/conservation loss is stated.

answers.answer: Sponsors I plays exactly one card from hand if action strength is at least its level and conditions are met. Alternatively, it advances the Break token by strength and pays that much money, even if fewer steps were needed to reach the final space. Sponsors II can play one or more cards when strength plus 1 is at least the sum of their levels; X-tokens can raise strength beyond 5. II cards may come from hand or from the display within reputation range for an added folder-number cost, with no display refill until turn end. Resolve cards one after another, completing each card's instant effects except 'after finishing' effects before the next. If using the Sponsors II break option, the money is paid twice. Thus, if only one step remains, Sponsors I still pays the full strength in money, and Sponsors II pays twice that amount.
answers.evidence: Sponsors I/II directly state level limits, source and folder cost, resolution order, delayed display refill, and full/double break-option money.

answers.answer: Break order: discard to hand limit (3, or 5 with the relevant university); return Multiplier, Venom, and Constriction tokens from Action cards; recall workers and replenish partner zoos/universities; discard display folders 1 and 2, slide remaining cards down and refill; then take income; finally reset the Break token. Kiosk income is 1 money per adjacent unique building, special enclosure (occupied or empty), occupied standard enclosure, or pavilion; empty standard enclosures do not count. Income is usually simultaneous; if an effect requires order, begin with the player who initiated the break (or the affected player closest to them) and proceed clockwise. Display cards taken during a turn are refilled only when the entire turn is complete, by sliding cards down and filling empty spaces from the deck; the summary does not specify a separate priority for several players taking display cards.
answers.evidence: Break procedure steps 1–6 give order, hand limits, display refill and income order; kiosk rule lists qualifying adjacent buildings. Display timing says refill after the entire turn.

answers.answer: At 2 conservation points, choose to upgrade an Action card or activate an additional worker. At 5 and 8, choose 5 money or the Bonus token next to that space. At 10, the first player to reach or exceed it makes all players discard one Final Scoring card; if nobody reaches 10 before game end, all discard one before final scoring. The game ends whenever a player's Appeal and Conservation counters are in the same scoring area or pass one another. The summary says the triggering player completes their turn and every other player takes one more turn; if triggered during a break, everyone takes one more turn. It does not explicitly clarify how the turn-completion instruction applies if the triggering gain occurs during another player's turn. Each Final Scoring card can add at most 4 conservation points. VP equals Appeal minus the lowest Appeal value in the scoring area containing the Conservation counter. Highest positive VP wins; ties go to the player who supported the most conservation projects, then tied players share the victory. The summary does not separately specify the timing rule for a gain during another player's turn beyond the stated trigger and last-turn rules.
answers.evidence: Scoring section lists milestone rewards, end trigger and extra turns, 4-point-per-card cap, VP formula and tiebreak. It does not clarify trigger turn completion for an effect during another player's turn.
